pr.title: Send scheduled MIDI and MIDI clock from field-audiod's audio callback (sequencer.md chunk 4)
pr.head: ce524011f914389e1be9c0bfe1b02fc89b58e215

summary: This layer adds the daemon’s scheduled MIDI output engine. Callers submit sample-positioned events through midi_out, choose a virtual source or destination, and close the output with midi_out_close.
The audio callback selects event windows; a sender delivers messages and MIDI clock. This layer builds on #233’s note model. The field seq projection and command callers remain later work.

cards.title: Timing vocabulary
cards.html:
• Schedule: MIDI bytes indexed by transport sample.
  • Lead: advance delivery by a configured number of samples.
  • Clock: tick and transport messages that follow playback and loop position.

cards.title: Review at ce52401
cards.html: Native build, typecheck, project validation, native self-test, and 24 focused tests pass, with one environmental skip. Two fake-sink probes expose loop-boundary and sustain-pedal teardown defects. Physical MIDI hardware and other operating systems were not tested.

groups.title: Define output schedules
groups.kicker: Start with the wire contract and ownership
intro: The TypeScript client validates schedules before sending them. The native model separates events, loop/clock settings, and output state so replacement schedules can retain their port.

groups.title: Select and deliver MIDI events
groups.kicker: Read the scheduling engine before its callers
intro: MidiOutputs takes callback windows, queues timestamped messages, and uses a sender thread for delivery. It tracks held notes and future note-offs so interruption can end notes whose release was queued ahead.

files.note: Follow selection, loop wrapping, sender delivery, and teardown in that order.

checks.text: P2: A wrap exactly at the window end returns before boundary cleanup and clock repositioning. A 1024-sample loop in 512-frame blocks reproduces repeated note-ons without the intervening note-off.
P2: Teardown tracks held keys but not CC64 sustain. A released note under the pedal survives stop, locate, or close; the probe observes no pedal release.

groups.title: Connect output to playback
groups.kicker: Transport position and callback timing feed selection
intro: The player passes playback windows, loop position, and timing margins to MIDI outputs. Live routing and ring input expose the information needed to avoid recording the daemon’s own virtual sources.

groups.title: Wire requests and monitor timestamps
groups.kicker: Daemon lifetime, IPC, and native build targets
intro: The server handles output requests and connection cleanup. The daemon owns output lifetime; the keys helper preserves source identity and timestamp information for monitoring.

groups.title: Exercise and document the engine
intro: The tests cover validation, port lifecycle, scheduling, clock, and CoreMIDI integration. Documentation records the daemon API and the completed engine slice while keeping the CLI projection as future work.

checks.text: Built native targets and ran the daemon self-test, typecheck, project check, and the MIDI output, helper, and MIDI recording suites: 24 passed, one environmental skip.
